summary: Round 2 re-review of all 9 units. All five round-1 fixes are verified: lidocaine example now gives 200 mg / 20 mL of 1% with 3 mg/kg (cap 200 mg) and 7 mg/kg with adrenaline (cap 500 mg) taught; ARDS text now credits prone positioning with survival benefit and says neuromuscular blockade has not shown routine survival benefit (ROSE); amiodarone 150 mg after the fifth shock is present in the lesson and example; the acid-base example is retitled and Winter's check is correct (1.5 x 11 + 8 = 24.5 +/- 2 mmHg; 3.4 kPa x 7.5 = 25.5 mmHg); the sepsis example continues boluses to 30 mL/kg (2700 mL) before a vasopressor. I recomputed every numeric key and worked-example number in Python (NEWS2 totals 8 and 9, MAP 63.3 and 52.7, delivered compression rate 84/min, compression fraction 83.3 per cent, P/F 212.5 and 116.7, PBW 57.0 kg / 342 mL and 75.1 kg / 451 mL, SOFA 6 and 12, urine 252 mL, paracetamol 200 and 225 mg/kg, rewarming 0.5 and 0.6 C/h, anion gaps 21 and 28, shock index 1.5, insulin 8 and 7 units/h, 30 mL/kg = 2040 and 2700 mL, GCS 12 and 9, CPP 63, lidocaine 20 mL and 9 mL) and all are correct; every MCQ has exactly one correct option matching the key. No tabs, control characters, literal \uXXXX text, CRLF problems, [object Object] or placeholder steps were found. Only two minor items remain. This is an AI review only; the course still needs an emergency medicine / intensive care subject-matter expert before clinical reliance, particularly for drug doses and current RCUK, NICE, JBDS and BNF thresholds.

issues.problem: The ABG pH 7.52, PaCO2 2.8 kPa (about 21 mmHg), HCO3- 22 mmol/L is not internally consistent under Henderson-Hasselbalch (these values give pH about 7.64; pH 7.52 with PaCO2 2.8 kPa implies HCO3- about 17 mmol/L). The key (respiratory alkalosis) is unaffected, but a student who checks the arithmetic will find the gas implausible.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the gas consistent, for example pH 7.52, PaCO2 3.4 kPa (about 25.5 mmHg), HCO3- 20 mmol/L (H-H gives about 7.52), or keep HCO3- 22 and PaCO2 2.8 kPa with pH about 7.6. Key remains respiratory alkalosis.

issues.problem: Objective 'Recognise and treat severe hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia' is met only with mechanisms and 'check current dose' hedges; no calcium, insulin-glucose or 3% saline regimen is given. Nothing stated is wrong, and withholding doses is a defensible safety choice.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add the UK Kidney Association hyperkalaemia and European/UK 3% saline bolus regimens with a 'verify locally' hedge, or reword the objective to 'describe the principles of treatment' so the objective matches the content.
